summary: A 1934 steel fire tower on the Kaibab Plateau's North Rim, with a cabin added in 1959 and a 1.3-mile trail up from the cabins. Current staffing is unconfirmed.

facts.design: Steel tower about 100 ft tall with a 7-ft square cab; wood-frame cabin at the base dating to 1959

access.note: Trail #51 and the upper parking area are open to the public. No source read says the tower itself is open to climbing; it is an active lookout.

visit.trail_note: Trail #51 is a steep 1.3-mile route from the Big Springs cabins up to the tower. The upper trailhead on Forest Road 454 has limited parking near the tower.

notes_for_editor: Build year, height and the cab size agree across the register, Wikipedia and the Kaibab album. Current staffing and any fire history are not documented in what I could read; the register's 'still in active use' has no date. The NRHP nomination PDF on NPGallery (NRIS 87002478) is listed as not yet digitized, so it could not be read. A tourism listing gives the trail as a 4-mile round trip, which conflicts with the Forest Service's 1.3-mile figure; I used the Forest Service page and did not open the listing. Access level 'restricted' is my reading of the sources, not a Forest Service rule. Brief's 'access: unknown' and 'height_m 30.5' are consistent with the sources; no corrections proposed.
